scope: Static managed metadata and CIL inspection of installed Bannerlord only; target code not loaded or executed; no native allocation, rendering, visual correctness, cleanup, FPS or thousands-visible proof.
observations: AgentVisuals is in TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.View namespace and Native module View assembly, not TaleWorlds.MountAndBlade.AgentVisuals. MBAgentVisuals and AgentVisualsData are in core MountAndBlade assembly.

AgentVisuals.Create calls its constructor; constructor calls MBAgentVisuals.CreateAgentVisuals(SceneData,name,MonsterData.EyeOffsetWrtHead), optionally SetEntity(EntityData), then Refresh. This constructor does not call Mission.SpawnAgent or construct managed Agent.

AgentVisuals.Refresh creates skeleton through MonsterExtensions.FillAnimationSystemData -> MBSkeletonExtensions.CreateWithActionSet -> MBAgentVisuals.SetSkeleton when ActionSet valid. It applies frame and assembles skin, armor and weapon meshes. Optional random progress sets animation phase.

CharacterDebugSpawner.InitWithCharacter is a shipped example using GameEntity.CreateEmpty(scene,false,true,true), CharacterCode equipment/body/race, FaceGen.GetBaseMonsterFromRace, AgentVisualsData, and AgentVisuals.Create without a Mission.SpawnAgent call.

CharacterDebugSpawner action set is MBGlobals.GetActionSetWithSuffix(monster,isFemale,"_facegen"); initial ActionCode is act_inventory_idle_start. It sets PoseAction with random progress and primes Skeleton.TickAnimationsAndForceUpdate(0.1, visual.GetGlobalFrame(), true). This is a character display example, not a validated marching soldier.

PopupSceneSpawnPoint.OnTick updates mount visuals first, then human visuals via Tick(mountOrNull, dt, false, 0); it additionally calls Skeleton.ForceUpdateBoneFrames. AgentVisuals.Tick delegates to MBAgentVisuals.Tick -> native IMBAgentVisuals.Tick.
AgentVisuals.SetAction sends channel zero to MBSkeletonExtensions.SetAgentActionChannel. GetVisuals().SetFrame(ref MatrixFrame) updates frame without an Agent argument.

PopupSceneSpawnPoint.Destroy calls Reset then nulls each visual. CharacterSpawner.OnRemoved calls Reset, GetVisuals().ManualInvalidate, and nulls field. MBAgentVisuals.Reset forwards to native IMBAgentVisuals.Reset; native deletion timing remains unproven.

AgentVisualsData copy constructor copies AgentVisuals and EntityData references, equipment and cached weapon entities. A data copy is not an independently owned render object and must not be treated as a safe pool clone.

MBAgentVisuals.BatchLastLodMeshes and SetLodAtlasShadingIndex are public wrappers into native callbacks. Their existence does not establish cross-soldier batching or caller-safe atlas slot allocation.

MetaMesh.BatchMultiMeshes(MetaMesh) and BatchMultiMeshesMultiple(List<MetaMesh>) send native pointers; GameEntity.CopyFrom and MetaMesh.CreateCopy exist. Metadata does not establish hardware instancing or shared skeleton animation.

No dedicated explicit GPU instancing API was found among inspected GameEntity/Mesh/MetaMesh/Skeleton public signatures. This statement covers only those types and does not prove renderer lacks instancing.

CreateAgentVisuals native callback wrapper accepts native scene pointer, UTF8 name, Vec3; returns NativeObjectPointer, constructs MBAgentVisuals only when Pointer nonzero, then decreases returned native reference count. Resource ownership must follow wrappers.
inferences: The first visible-soldier prototype can use existing AgentVisuals with an explicitly owned Scene/GameEntity, avoiding a managed Agent allocation path. Native independence from the 2040 Agent pool still needs direct evidence.
Render-only proxies need their own transforms, action choice, coarse ground alignment and visibility. They do not inherit agent collision, damage, navigation, AI or campaign semantics.

Use a bounded medium-distance animated visual tier first, with real Agents near the player. If skeleton cost limits population, a farther tier needs shared poses or baked mesh/impostor batches. Existing batching method names alone do not establish that far tier is available.

Compare frozen pose visuals against fully animated visuals to isolate skeleton/animation cost, then test shadows, material variety, cloth and face generation independently. Face/weapon caching should be explicit and measured.
Do not copy the native Agent limit check or raise it to claim visibility scaling; test distinct render-only allocations, simultaneous screen visibility and frame time.
unknowns: Whether MBAgentVisuals.CreateAgentVisuals allocates from any fixed capacity shared with Agents, renderer atlas pages, skinning buffers or skeletons.

Whether Reset removes the entity/skeleton immediately, whether separately supplied entities need additional removal, and safe order for scene shutdown. Shipped callers suggest lifecycle but do not prove standalone mission ownership.
Whether SetAgentLodZeroOrMax selects maximum geometry, minimal geometry, distance-independent binary LOD, or other semantics. Boolean name alone is insufficient for optimization.
Capacity, thread affinity, lifetime and ownership of SetLodAtlasShadingIndex; do not invent one atlas index per proxy or reuse indices without native verification.
Exact native behavior of BatchLastLodMeshes and MetaMesh batching with animated/skinned geometry; no GPU draw-call capture or native renderer analysis performed in this subtask.
Performance and visible fidelity for 1000, 2000, 5000 or more proxies; no runtime or screenshot capture performed.
Moving/combat action set choice and weapon pose behavior in a mission; _facegen example is suitable for initial construction evidence only.
Safe promotion/demotion while preserving identity and avoiding simultaneous proxy/Agent duplicate visuals; campaign casualties and combat simulation remain separate.

firstPrototypeContract.update: Keep simulation transforms separate. Set native visual frame, update selected action/phase, tick animation at a measured budget, set visibility. Begin on known scene/main update context; do not assume native operations are safe on worker threads.
firstPrototypeContract.cleanup: Follow selected shipped ownership example: Reset visual, invalidate native wrapper if appropriate, clear references; explicitly determine separately owned entity removal behavior before recycling or mission exit.
measurements: Mission.AllAgents count before and after proxy allocation
Proxy creation success and native pointer/entity validity
Screenshots at fixed battlefield camera proving simultaneous visible soldiers
CPU/GPU/frame time percentiles and memory at 0/128/512/1024/2048/4096 proxies
Frozen vs animated, shadows on/off, identical vs varied equipment
Repeated create/destroy cycles and clean scene exit without retained entities
firstPrototypeContract.construction: Use a fresh AgentVisualsData for each owned visual. Fill Equipment, BodyProperties, Race, Frame, SkeletonType, Scene, Monster, ActionSet, ActionCode, colors and an optional separately owned empty GameEntity. Call AgentVisuals.Create(data,uniqueName,false,false,false). Start with known _facegen action set and inventory idle for construction proof; marching uses a separately verified action set.
firstPrototypeContract.status: proposal grounded in shipped APIs; not implemented or run by this subtask
firstPrototypeContract.claimGate: Report thousands visible only after an actual on-screen populated battlefield capture and count evidence. Report playable only with measured stable frame time and correctness under movement.
